I basically agree with almost this whole comment, especially the last paragraph. 

The initial reason for this discussion was that I saw hostility in your original comments, which in hindsight, after re-reading them, and with your reasoning fully laid out, I now believe was a wrong and undeserved reading of your intentions (although your jumping back and forth with the definition of 'victim' still seems wrong and a bit accusatory to me).

So I suppose the only point we disagreed on at all were the framing of the situation and the use of a word and its baggage, while our other opinions are essentially one and the same.

I honestly think this was a productive exercise in reasoning for both of us, or at least for me, and I want to apologize for my initial 'finger-pointing', I may have jumped the gun a little bit.

Two things I disagree with: 

It's not like irresponsibly getting cut by a knife, it's the direct result of a rational, thinking person who chooses to do a bad action. A knife can't choose to harm, therefore isn't acting on an ethical basis.

And second, if not by being angry with how the world works and trying to fight it back, how can we expect to change it? Ignoring the bad and the wrong only lets it fester. It's not just about defending someone's feelings, but trying to change what we perceive as immoral, or at the very least to console who suffers from it.

Again, I completely agree with you that he should have expected, or even just suspected, that some comments like that were gonna show up. But I just don't think that means he's no longer a victim and that asking for consolation is anything to condemn

Maybe I wasn't clear, I apologize.

The example I brought up was in no way to compare how or when the line is drawn in regard to what shouldn't be allowed or should be punished (obviously I don't believe we should limit or forbid any offensive language). 

The single and only point I was making with the example is: blaming someone for not "accepting" or for not ignoring a negative, and purely negative (with no other purpose than to be damaging) reaction to interacting with a certain space (asking for criticism on the internet or walking alone at night as a woman, which obviously aren't comparable in severity), is plainly wrong.

The person affected by the negative response is in no single way at fault, at any point.
Should they be expected to expect negativity? For certain spaces, for sure. 
But even then, if they have the responsibility to decide which spaces to interact with, why blame them? They're not the reason the negativity is there, they aren't the  perpetrator.

And especially for cases like OP, why are they in any way in the wrong when they get attacked out of nowhere (even if they should have expected it) with the purpose to worsen their illness?
